verdicts.evidence: /\/+$/ -> /\/$/ strips only ONE trailing slash: normalizeForPath('src/a//') -> 'src/a/' (base 'src/a'), 'src/a///' -> 'src/a//', 'dir///' -> 'dir//'. The leftover slash reaches selector.for in rules --json --for and the glob match, and normalizeForPath is also the pattern validator in territory-map.ts. No layer went red.

verdicts.evidence: The sentinel is appended instead of stripping the trailing slash: normalizeForPath('a/b/') -> 'a/bStryker was here!', 'src/a//' -> 'src/aStryker was here!', and '/' -> 'Stryker was here!' instead of null, so a bare root stops being rejected. The sibling literal on the same line (.replace(/^\.\//, "")) measures as a hole too ('./src/a.ts' -> 'Stryker was here!src/a.ts', './' -> 'Stryker was here!'). No layer went red.

verdicts.evidence: Dropping ^ makes any letter-plus-colon anywhere in the path read as a Windows drive: normalizeForPath('aC:/x') returned null (base 'aC:/x') and `runward rules --for "src/a:b.ts"` exited 2 with 'Cannot ask about ... paths must be project-relative' where the baseline exits 0 and answers. An exit-code flip on a legitimate project-relative path. No layer went red.
